Subject: Expedited: data residency exception & SOW edits for Bluefield order form

Evan / Marc —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, Bluefield wants to sign and start the pilot in July but needs two small but critical edits before legal will sign: (1) a limited data residency carve-out that allows staging in us-east for the first 90 days, and (2) a short implementation schedule tweak in the SOW (Phase 1 ramp +30 days).

I attached the current Order Form and SOW with the sections flagged. Can Legal and Sales Ops review the redlines below and confirm whether we can accommodate the residency exception with the following constraints:
- Residency carve-out limited to non-production staging environment only
- Full production must be in the customer-selected region by day 91
- Audit logging and retention unchanged (we can offer a 45-day log retention for staging)

Timeline: Bluefield is asking for sign-off by 6/30 EOD — I know that is tight, but they want to begin procurement and provisioning next week. Please push any redlines back into the doc or reply inline.

Attachments: OrderForm_Bluefield_v2.docx, SOW_Implementation_Plan_v2.xlsx

Subject: Re: Expedited: data residency exception & SOW edits for Bluefield order form

Connor —

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read here — we can offer a limited, timeboxed residency exception for staging with some guardrails. Proposed approach:

1) Add a new clause to the Order Form (Section X): "Residency Exception — Staging." Suggested language (short):
   "Notwithstanding the Data Residency provisions in the MSA, Customer and Redwood agree that Customer may use a Redwood-managed staging environment located in the us-east-1 region for a period not to exceed 90 days from activation for non-production testing. By day 91, Customer shall transition production workloads to the region specified in the Order Form. Redwood will provide reasonable assistance for migration at Customer's request."

2) Add a sentence in SOW Phase 1 implementation timeline: "Phase 1 go-live may be extended by up to 30 calendar days to accommodate residency-related provisioning; parties will confirm the revised dates within 10 business days of signature."

3) Logging & retention: we cannot change corporate-wide retention policy, but will make an exception to guarantee 45-day log retention for the staging environment.

4) Pricing: there is an operational cost to maintaining a temporary staging carve-out and additional migration support. Recommend a one-time implementation surcharge of 5% on the Phase 1 implementation fees (ref: Fee_Table_Bluefield_v3.csv). If Sales approves, Legal will add a one-line fee of "Residency exception support — one-time" to the Order Form.

I attached a redline (Redline_OrderForm_SOW_karthik_v1.docx) with the proposed edits. If Sales agrees to the fee, I can incorporate final language and route to DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Contracts & Legal Operations

- Accept proposed residency carve-out language in principle

Connor / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for drafting language. Bluefield can accept the staging residency carve-out in principle, and we are OK with the one-time 5% surcharge for implementation support. A couple of housekeeping asks before we sign:

- Please include explicit wording around SLA for the staging environment (uptime and support response goals) — we just need 99.5% SLA during the 90-day staging window.
- Confirm the audit log retention guarantee of 45 days in the SOW and add a short paragraph on access for Bluefield's security team (read-only access to logs via request).
- We also request a 30-day ramp extension for Phase 2 deliverables (we'll provide proposed dates in the morning).

If Legal can fold those three bullets into the final redline we will proceed with signature via DocuSign. Please send the DocuSign packet to my attention (evan.strauss@bluefieldsys.com).
